WITH order_type_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    o.ordertune,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) as type_count
  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN orderexecutions oe ON o.recordvault = oe.ordersmark
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
type_shares AS (
  SELECT 
    ordertune,
    type_count,
    CAST(type_count AS REAL) / SUM(type_count) OVER () as share
  FROM order_type_counts
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM type_shares
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    ts.type_count,
    ts.share,
    oa.avg_share
  FROM type_shares ts
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
  WHERE ts.share > oa.avg_share
)
SELECT 
  SUM(type_count) as sum_count,
  AVG(share) as avg_share_above_average,
  AVG(share - avg_share) as avg_excess
FROM above_average

assumptions.assumption: NULL values in ordertune are treated as a distinct order-type group (standard SQL GROUP BY semantics). The phrase 'missing order type forms its own group' is interpreted as NULL being included.
'Strictly above' means share > avg_share (not >=), as the word 'strictly' indicates a strict inequality.
